turns.q:
Your response was: "Looked at it. Checkout flow. Nearly missed the submit button. It barely registered visually — took a moment to find the action I needed."

We want to understand what you meant by "nearly missed the submit button", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The low visual contrast between the "Place Order" button and the background.
B) The placement of the "Place Order" button at the very bottom of the layout.
C) The proximity of the "Place Order" button to the "Continue Shopping" button.
D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
In what way does the visual style of that "Place Order" button compare to the "Continue Shopping" button above it?
turns.a: Two buttons. Bottom of the screen. One is dark and visible — 'Continue Shopping.' The other is barely there. Nearly the same color as the background.

turns.q: If a developer built this layout exactly as shown, how would that lack of distinction between the two buttons affect someone's ability to identify the primary action?
turns.a: 'Place Order.' Faint. Label barely there. Easy to overlook — didn't register where it should.

turns.q: If a user is scanning this page for the first time, does that lack of visibility make the "Place Order" action harder to find entirely, or just less obvious once they reach the bottom?
turns.a: Same. Eye went elsewhere. Didn't pull.

turns.q: What would the correct version of that "Place Order" button area actually look like to ensure it captures attention immediately?
turns.a: More visible. Bigger. Has to stand out — can't be the one you scan past.

turns.q: What would you never accept as a workaround if this layout went to build with the "Place Order" button in its current state?
turns.a: Solid high-contrast fill on 'Place Order' — a real color, not gray. WCAG AA minimum: 4.5:1 contrast ratio for the label text. Label up to at least 14–16px. Gray on gray at 12px reads as disabled — it fails WCAG AA and it fails as a primary CTA. Fix: brand color fill, white label text, readable size. One button. That's it.
